reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust periodic pattern with a fundamental period of ~18 points, confirmed across all candidates. Normal behavior consists of sharp, narrow V-shaped troughs (depth ~0.5–1.0 standardized units) alternating with broader, flatter plateaus or gentle slopes at higher levels (~1.0–1.5). Peaks are typically rounded or flat-topped rather than尖锐; amplitude (90th percentile range) scales with window length: ~1.5 for 1-cycle, ~2.3–2.4 for 3-cycle, and ~3.0 for 5-cycle windows, indicating consistent waveform scaling. Baseline level varies modestly across segments (median from -0.27 to +1.21), but local stability within each cycle is high—no sustained drift (>0.03 per point) except in candidate 0, which shows a slight negative slope. Noise is low: MAD ranges 0.20–0.74, with roughness (local variability) lowest in candidate 1 (0.135) and highest in candidate 2 (0.674), suggesting candidate 2 may contain minor contamination or higher-frequency perturbations. Trough timing is regular (every ~18 points), though minor phase jitter (<2 pts) occurs. Boundary truncation is minimal; all intervals are cleanly aligned to cycle boundaries per the reference_cycle_plan. Acceptable variation includes moderate baseline shifts, small slope deviations (<±0.02/pt), and occasional flattened peaks—but not persistent monotonic trends, excessive roughness (>0.7), or abnormally deep/sharp troughs beyond ~1.0 unit.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (18-pt) segment showing highly regular, symmetric V-troughs every ~6 pts (3 per cycle), with sharp minima near 0.0 and flat plateaus near 1.2–1.5. Slight negative slope (-0.016/pt) and unusually high median (1.21) suggest it may be offset upward relative to other candidates; morphology is clean but possibly non-representative of typical baseline.

Three-cycle (54-pt) segment with well-defined, moderately deep troughs (~-0.5 to 0.0), gentle slopes, and stable plateaus near 1.0–1.5. Very low roughness (0.135) and near-zero slope (+0.005/pt) indicate high stability; waveform repeats cleanly with minimal distortion. Best exemplar of canonical normal behavior.

Three-cycle segment with similar trough depth and periodicity as candidate 1, but noticeably higher roughness (0.674) and steeper negative slope (-0.033/pt). Contains more jagged transitions and minor irregularities in peak shape; may reflect localized disturbance or mild contamination. Still preserves core periodic structure.

Five-cycle (90-pt) segment showing scaled-up version of the motif: deeper troughs (~-0.5 to -0.7), higher peaks (~2.5), and broader plateaus. Amplitude scales linearly with cycles; slope is nearly flat (-0.0015/pt). Contains one anomalous steep rise near pt 2788–2791, but overall morphology aligns with consensus. Most comprehensive view of long-term stability.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 1 (3P, low roughness) as primary template for matching queries with clean, stable morphology. Use candidate 0 for queries with single-cycle length or high baseline offset. Candidate 3 is optimal for multi-cycle (≥4 cycles) queries due to its extended context and amplitude scaling. Avoid relying on candidate 2 for baseline definition unless query shows similarly elevated roughness and negative drift—treat its features as potential anomaly indicators rather than normative.
uncertainties: Exact baseline level is not fixed across segments; normality tolerates ±0.5 shift in median without anomaly implication.
Whether the slight negative trend in candidate 0 and 2 is intrinsic or contamination remains ambiguous without labels.
The origin of elevated roughness in candidate 2—is it sensor noise, process variation, or incipient fault—is unresolved.
Phase alignment tolerance (±2 pts) is inferred but unverified; minor jitter may be normal.
